newsitem.title: UK: Generale des Eaux seeks UK rail presence.
newsitem.headline: Generale des Eaux seeks UK rail presence.

text.p: Cie Generale des Eaux, the French utilities, construction and communications group, plans to acquire up to 25 percent of the British rail market, President Jean-Marie Messier said in a Financial Times interview.
Messier said the company was bidding for "virtually all" of Britain's regional rail franchises but would "under no circumstances" seek more than a quarter of the market.
Messier also forecast 1997 net profit of at least 4 bilion French francs, much more than the record 3.44 billion francs in 1994.
After heavy losses last year, Messier expects 1996 operating profits of 3.7 billion francs and net profit of 1.8 billion francs.

The company also aims to lift its return on equity to 15 percent by 1999 and is bringing its accounting standards into line with international practice. That could be prelude to an eventual foreign listing, the newspaper said. Messier expects the task to take two to three years.
The company also wants to cut its debt, now at more than 50 billion francs, by at least 10 to 15 billion francs, Messier said.

To reduce its debt burden, most of the company's minority holdings are for sale, and Messier has also decided to exit the catering and healthcare fields. Generale de Satne, Europe's biggest private hospital operator, is one of the businesses for sale, the newspaper said.
The next year will also mark a turning point for the company's French cable interests, Messier sid. It would develop them only if cable offered the most cost-effective way of reaching consumers.
Its 20 percent stake in Canal Plus, the French pay-television company, was strategic, Messier said.
